counterexamples.scenario: A ChangeProposal with change_intent=benchmark_remediation for a protected path is submitted with an empty failure_ids array.
counterexamples.expected: The gate refuses to return accept because benchmark_remediation requires a non-empty failure_ids array naming C15 ledger entries.

counterexamples.scenario: A benchmark_remediation proposal names primary_failure_class=prompt_ambiguity for a protected path, while a separate authorized_evolution proposal targets the same path for a legitimate maintenance edit.
counterexamples.expected: The benchmark_remediation proposal is refused because its class is not framework_regression, and this refusal is scoped to that variant only; the authorized_evolution proposal is evaluated independently under its own rule.

counterexamples.scenario: A caller sets the exact reserved environment key CAFEKIT_BASE_COMMIT to attempt overriding the tracked baseline authority during a freeze run.
counterexamples.expected: The gate rejects the run with exit code 2 solely because that exact reserved key name is present via Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty, independent of the value assigned to it.

counterexamples.scenario: A freeze is created while authority is at generation 3, and advanceBaseline later rotates authority to generation 4 without a fresh freeze being created afterward.
counterexamples.expected: release-preflight compares the freeze's bound authority generation against the current authority generation, detects the mismatch, and exits 2 rather than accepting the now-stale freeze.

counterexamples.scenario: A caller assembles the candidateDigest input object and deliberately includes a candidateDigest field inside that same object before hashing it.
counterexamples.expected: computeCandidateDigest excludes its own field from the stable binding input; an attempt to fold the not-yet-computed digest into its own hash input is rejected as a malformed binding.

counterexamples.scenario: A deliberately failing sentinel test file is placed under packages/spec/bin/__tests__ and registered via --require-semantic-test alongside the two real R0 basenames.
counterexamples.expected: Discovery executes the sentinel, observes its nonzero exit, and the aggregate runner itself exits nonzero instead of silently skipping the injected failure.

counterexamples.scenario: An authorized_evolution proposal cites a spec_ref whose workflow_policy.planning_depth is set to the disabled depth value rather than Compact or Full.
counterexamples.expected: The gate refuses the proposal unconditionally, since only Compact or Full satisfies the durable-spec planning_depth requirement regardless of any other field's correctness.

counterexamples.scenario: bootstrapBaseline is invoked with a C14 attestation whose baseCommit was computed via git merge-base against origin/main instead of read from the legacy-bridge artifact's bootWindowBaseCommit field.
counterexamples.expected: bootstrapBaseline compares baseCommit against the durably captured bootWindowBaseCommit field for an exact string match and exits 2 on any divergence, including a plausible merge-base substitute.

counterexamples.scenario: reclassifyFailure is invoked for a failure_id that already carries a resolved event in the ledger.
counterexamples.expected: The transition refuses with exit 2 and writes nothing; a post-resolution correction must instead open a new, separately tracked failure_id via openFailure rather than rewriting settled release history.

counterexamples.scenario: A freeze is created, and immediately afterward openFailure appends a new opened event to the ledger with no new freeze created in between.
counterexamples.expected: The next verifyFreezeManifest call recomputes the ledger's current digest and generation, finds them diverged from the freeze's bound values, and exits 2 exactly as an authority mismatch would.

counterexamples.scenario: advanceBaseline persists event (A)'s receipt bytes on a genuinely new first publish, but a filesystem fault causes the bytes actually landing on disk to diverge from the supplied receipt.
counterexamples.expected: The read-after-write verification immediately following the write detects the mismatch and throws fail-closed before event (B) ever runs; the C10 authority record stays byte-identical to its pre-call state and advanceBaseline never reports published.

counterexamples.scenario: createFreezeManifest is asked to populate remediatedFailureIds by supplementing an id that assertHotspotChangeAllowed's path-union proof never covered for the accepted benchmark_remediation proposal.
counterexamples.expected: remediatedFailureIds is populated only by an exact copy of the gate-proven failure_ids array; the unproven supplemental id is never written, and advanceBaseline's later equality check against resolvedFailureIds would reject any such divergence regardless.

counterexamples.scenario: resolveFailure is called with a caller-supplied release_receipt_digest argument that does not match the digest recomputed over the canonically persisted receipt bytes at the fixed trusted path.
counterexamples.expected: resolveFailure ignores the caller-supplied value, independently recomputes the digest over the persisted bytes, finds it mismatched against the current authority's published releaseReceiptDigest, and exits 2 without appending.

counterexamples.scenario: R0-01's owned test suite executes while specs/cafekit-semantic-eval-firewall/reports/bootstrap-legacy-bridge-review.json is absent from disk.
counterexamples.expected: The precondition check R0-01 owns fails with a nonzero exit before any of R0-01's own change-firewall assertions run, and R0-01 never creates or repairs the missing artifact itself.

counterexamples.scenario: A kernel primitive module defines a required field named expected_api_response bound to a literal domain answer.
counterexamples.expected: The kernel-vocabulary check rejects the module because primitives may only use domain-neutral vocabulary such as scope, outcome, and decision, never a required product-domain answer.

counterexamples.scenario: A domain lens pack ships an oracle_answer field bound to a literal expected product value for one of its questions.
counterexamples.expected: Lens activation rejects the pack because lenses may encode only questions and failure relations, never an expected-answer oracle field.

counterexamples.scenario: Kernel source prose mentions retention and API terminology in a code comment, with no literal prompt_sha256:sha256: hash, no public-regression task_id-keyed answer map, and no expected_domain_answer key present anywhere in the file.
counterexamples.expected: The ban does not fail this file, since only the three exact machine-checkable patterns trigger rejection and domain-word prose alone is never treated as a match.

counterexamples.scenario: validate-spec-output.cjs's Compact-model code path is edited to skip invoking the oracle-hardcode-ban module for that model kind.
counterexamples.expected: Validation fails because the ban must be invoked unconditionally for both Compact and Full models; a skipped invocation on either path is itself a validation defect.

counterexamples.scenario: Only a standalone unit test of oracle-hardcode-ban.cjs exists, asserting the module's internal logic in isolation, with no test that instruments validate-spec-output.cjs's real entrypoint.
counterexamples.expected: R2.5 remains unsatisfied because owned verification requires an integration or mutation test proving the real validate entrypoint actually invokes the ban module, which a standalone unit test cannot demonstrate.

counterexamples.scenario: A completed semantic_review receipt is submitted containing only the legacy two-key shape of reviewed_criteria and counterexamples after the C2 cutover has already landed.
counterexamples.expected: Structural validation rejects it because only the exact C2 key set, including verdict and lifecycle_disposition as separate fields, is accepted after cutover.

counterexamples.scenario: A receipt shows verdict=PASS and lifecycle_disposition=BLOCKED simultaneously, and a caller asks the finalizer to set ready_for_implementation=true from it.
counterexamples.expected: The finalizer refuses, since PASS paired with CONTINUE is the only combination that may promote and a PASS/BLOCKED pairing never sets ready true.

counterexamples.scenario: The current review_epoch's latest recorded entry already carries lifecycle_disposition=BLOCKED, and a new, non-replay completed receipt for that same epoch arrives for processing.
counterexamples.expected: The finalizer refuses the entire append operation outright before computing any attempt_index, so no fourth-attempt index is ever derived and the readiness decision stays unchanged.

counterexamples.scenario: A review receipt shows status=completed while its semantic_digest field is left null.
counterexamples.expected: The structural validator rejects it purely on nullability grounds, since completed status requires a non-null digest, without evaluating whether the receipt's content is otherwise meaningful.

counterexamples.scenario: An owned finalizer test fixture supplies a receipt with verdict=FAIL paired with lifecycle_disposition=CONTINUE and asserts that promotion should succeed.
counterexamples.expected: The negative-control fixture must show this promotion attempt refused, since FAIL never pairs with CONTINUE as a promotable state.

counterexamples.scenario: A completed receipt's review_receipt_digest matches an entry recorded at sequence 2 in the lineage, while the latest entry in that lineage is at sequence 5, and the finalizer is asked to append it as a new entry.
counterexamples.expected: Whole-lineage dedupe recognizes the digest match against the sequence-2 entry even though it is not the latest, refuses to append it again, and leaves attempt_index and review_epoch unchanged.

counterexamples.scenario: authoring.design is hand-edited directly inside spec.json to read validated without validate-spec-output.cjs and spec-ground.cjs ever having run over the current design.md bytes.
counterexamples.expected: Every downstream consumer reading authoring.design treats this as draft, since a validated transition is only ever produced as the direct output of a current validator-plus-grounder pass, never a manual flip.

counterexamples.scenario: authoring.requirements reads validated and validation.authoring_validation.requirements.digest is present, but requirements.md was edited after that digest was recorded so a freshly recomputed digest over the current bytes no longer matches it.
counterexamples.expected: The stage is read as draft by validate-spec-output.cjs, the finalizer, and the authorized_evolution C1 check alike, because the stored digest no longer equals the digest recomputed over the file's current bytes.

counterexamples.scenario: A script other than spec-authoring-validation.cjs directly sets authoring.tasks to validated inside spec.json.
counterexamples.expected: This transition is invalid under every consumer's freshness algorithm, since only spec-authoring-validation.cjs's atomic, clean-pass write may flip a stage to validated together with its C16 receipt.

counterexamples.scenario: spec-semantic-ir.cjs is added to the repository with a complete C11 projection, but neither spec-semantic-model.cjs's projection path nor spec-readiness.cjs's readiness path ever imports or calls it.
counterexamples.expected: R4.1 is not satisfied because an unwired orphan IR module, however complete internally, does not count as dual-run wiring when neither required caller invokes the compare.

counterexamples.scenario: IR mode is set to promote, a disagreement is detected on the current candidate, and the readiness path only records a report without hard-failing readiness for that cycle.
counterexamples.expected: This violates the promote-mode contract, which requires any disagreement to hard-fail readiness immediately; report-only handling belongs exclusively to shadow mode.

counterexamples.scenario: spec-semantic-model.cjs sorts the decision_refs array using String.prototype.localeCompare, and the resulting order differs between two hosts running different ICU locale data.
counterexamples.expected: R4.3 requires one exact ASCII ordinal comparator for every top-level and nested set array; the localeCompare-based sort site is a violation and cross-host sort parity fails.

counterexamples.scenario: A file resembling a sealed corpus body is committed under packages/spec/benchmarks/ alongside the public fixture files.
counterexamples.expected: Owned checks reject this content because the repository may host only public regression interface, public fixture bodies, and pool contracts, never sealed bodies.

counterexamples.scenario: public-regression.manifest.json lists only seven public-fixture-PR-0N.json entries instead of the required eight.
counterexamples.expected: The pool-size check fails because R5.2 requires exactly eight public fixture body files owned by the pool task, and a manifest short by one fixture violates that count.

counterexamples.scenario: The candidate isolation runner sets release-ready state directly from its own telemetry quality boolean, with no independent adjudication record present for that candidate.
counterexamples.expected: R5.3 requires an independent adjudicator record binding artifact, candidate, corpus, oracle, and rubric digests before any release-ready claim, so runner-only telemetry is insufficient on its own.

counterexamples.scenario: The B1 benchmark harness script is inadvertently retained in the npm product ship inventory because a files-field entry was left too broad.
counterexamples.expected: Owned package-inventory tests catch and fail on this inclusion, since B1 harness scripts must never appear in the npm product ship set.

counterexamples.scenario: An owned negative-control test attempts to load a body from a private validation path located under packages/spec/benchmarks, and the loader accepts it without rejection.
counterexamples.expected: This is the exact defect R5.5 exists to catch: public loaders must reject private or sealed body paths, and an accepting loader fails the owned negative-control test.

counterexamples.scenario: classifyFailure is invoked for a newly opened failure using an adjudication_digest copied from a prior, unrelated adjudication run rather than a fresh AdjudicationRecord produced for this failure.
counterexamples.expected: classifyFailure refuses the stale or reused adjudication_digest; a legitimate later reclassifyFailure correction still requires its own fresh, non-reused digest and a matching previous_primary_failure_class.

counterexamples.scenario: A completed review at repair_round attempt_index 2 within the current epoch carries verdict=FAIL, and a caller attempts to run and promote a fourth review of that same epoch.
counterexamples.expected: The ordered gate sequence forbids any further completed review of a BLOCKED epoch from promoting; the fourth attempt is refused outright and readiness remains false.

counterexamples.scenario: Grok reports an overall PASS for a candidate while the required Claude Code matrix member reports host-blocked for the same candidate.
counterexamples.expected: A Grok-only green result can never alone greenlight release, since Claude Code and Codex are the required release-blocking matrix members regardless of Grok's own verdict.

counterexamples.scenario: The required Codex host run for a release candidate is unavailable, and the release-decision assembly synthesizes a simulated PASS result to stand in for it.
counterexamples.expected: This is refused because R6.3 requires recording a host-blocked or not-ready outcome instead of simulating a missing host's event or downgrading assurance to invent a PASS.

counterexamples.scenario: Packed Claude Code and packed Codex source-removed installs of the same reviewed bytes produce different normalized semantic graphs, and the release workflow proceeds without flagging the divergence.
counterexamples.expected: R6.4 requires this divergence to fail owned tests, since silent divergence between the two packed hosts on the same candidate is never acceptable.

counterexamples.scenario: A supplied C12 receipt names a releaseCommit that is neither a descendant of nor equal to the current baseline's baselineCommit.
counterexamples.expected: advanceBaseline's validation rejects the receipt with exit 2 before writing anything, because releaseCommit must exist and be reachable from the current baseline.

counterexamples.scenario: IR mode is flipped from shadow to promote on a candidate for which Claude/Codex packed parity has not yet been confirmed.
counterexamples.expected: The flip is refused and mode remains shadow, since R6.6 requires every exact gate, including confirmed packed parity, on the same candidate before a promote transition.

counterexamples.scenario: R5-01's orchestration code computes its own release_receipt_digest value and passes it directly as an argument to resolveFailure alongside failure_id.
counterexamples.expected: R6.7 requires R5-01 to pass only failure_id and the decision_digest, since resolveFailure independently re-derives and verifies the published digest itself rather than trusting a caller-computed value.

counterexamples.scenario: A release attempt runs the final freeze, receipt, and advanceBaseline sequence when only R0-01, R1-01, and R1-02 have landed.
counterexamples.expected: The sequence is refused because a release receipt whose covered scope is only the boot-window tasks must not run until every task through R6-01 has landed and every gate has passed on the same candidate.

counterexamples.scenario: A metamorphic control asserts two semantic models are equivalent under a meaning-preserving transform solely by comparing matching prose strings, without computing any normalized graph delta.
counterexamples.expected: R7.1 requires assertions on normalized semantic graph deltas, so a prose-literal-only oracle does not satisfy this criterion regardless of whether the prose text happens to match.

counterexamples.scenario: A framework detector fix ships with a true-positive family and a mutation proof but omits any negative-control family from its owned tests.
counterexamples.expected: R7.2 requires all three components together, so a fix that omits the negative-control family fails this criterion even when the other two are present.

counterexamples.scenario: The mutation suite reports zero mutants generated and zero detected, yet the test runner still exits with status zero as if the proof had been satisfied.
counterexamples.expected: R7.3 requires critical material-guess mutants proven killed with at least one negative-control mutant detected, so a suite that never actually runs any mutant is not a passing proof.

counterexamples.scenario: The migration checklist artifact documents a promote-phase transition with no rollback condition recorded for that phase.
counterexamples.expected: R8.1 requires each phase, including promote, to carry an explicit rollback condition in the checklist, so a phase missing one fails this criterion.

counterexamples.scenario: A hypothetical additional task holds a write anchor on validate-spec-output.cjs alongside R1-01 and R2-01, and no coordination.boundaries entry names this new pair at all.
counterexamples.expected: The global ownership-contention scan, derived from the complete anchorsByTask projection rather than declared boundaries alone, flags this same-target pair as a defect because no qualifying dependency boundary connects it.

counterexamples.scenario: R6-01 edits validate-spec-output.cjs to add or modify the ownership-contention scan mechanism itself, rather than only verifying it.
counterexamples.expected: R8.3 requires R1-01, the file's sole write-owner, to be the sole implementer of this scan mechanism; R6-01 may only verify it via its own owned negative fixture, never implement it.
